# Verdant Engine

> Commercial 3D browser and WebAssembly game engine in Rust (`crates/verdant-core`) with archetype ECS, SAH BVH culling, procedural terrain and L-system flora, PBR materials, W3C WGSL shader validation, Khronos glTF 2.0 binary export, 60Hz symplectic Euler physics, spatial audio, SHA-256 world snapshots, and verified cosmological Builder statics.

## Documentation

- [Verdant Engine documentation](https://afflom.github.io/verdant-engine/docs/): Build fast 3D games and interactive worlds for the web and Rust.
- [Build your first 3D world](https://afflom.github.io/verdant-engine/docs/getting-started/): Create a Rust 3D scene, step rigid-body physics, and export a binary asset.
- [Author terrain, shaders, and spatial audio](https://afflom.github.io/verdant-engine/docs/guides/custom-game-world/): Build 3D terrain meshes, check GPU shaders, and mix 3D sound.
- [Verdant Core API reference](https://afflom.github.io/verdant-engine/docs/reference/engine-api/): Look up engine modules, core types, error codes, and 60fps frame budgets.
- [World expansion and architectural statics](https://afflom.github.io/verdant-engine/docs/explanation/cosmology-and-builders/): Learn why natural biomes and constructed monuments emerge in strict order.
- [Powering Verdant Resonance in the browser](https://afflom.github.io/verdant-engine/docs/case-studies/verdant-resonance/): See how Verdant Engine runs a 60fps 3D sanctuary with clutter-free controls.
